item.question: Can you use the numbers marked to find the angle without counting the number of markings? Here, OT and OS pass through the numbers 20 and 55 on the outer scale. How many units of 1 degree are contained between these two arms? Can subtraction be used here?
steps_tex: Read both arms on the same (outer) scale: $20$ and $55$
item.answer_tex: Yes. $55 - 20$ gives $35\text{ units}$, so the angle between $OT$ and $OS$ is $35^\circ$. Yes, subtraction can be used.

concept_name: Half a circle and a quarter: 180° and 90°

item.question: Make your own protractor by paper folding. 1. Draw a circle of a convenient radius on a sheet of paper. Cut out the circle (Fig. 2.13). A circle or one full turn is 360°. 2. Fold the circle to get two equal halves and cut it through the crease to get a semicircle. Write '0°' in the bottom right corner of the semicircle. 3. Fold the semi-circular sheet in half as shown in Fig. 2.15 to form a quarter circle. 4. Fold the sheet again as shown in Figs. 2.16 and 2.17. 5. Continue with another half fold as shown in Fig. 2.18. 6. Unfold and mark the creases as OB, OC, ..., etc., as shown in Fig. 2.19 and Fig. 2.20.
steps: Circle = 360°; half fold gives 180° (write 180° at left bottom corner)
item.answer: Open-ended craft. Resulting marks on the semicircle: 0°, 22.5°, 45°, 67.5°, 90°, 112.5°, 135°, 157.5°, 180°.
item.text:
Worked example: Make your own protractor by paper folding. 1. Draw a circle of a convenient radius on a sheet of paper. Cut out the circle (Fig. 2.13). A circle or one full turn is 360°. 2. Fold the circle to get two equal halves and cut it through the crease to get a semicircle. Write '0°' in the bottom right corner of the semicircle. 3. Fold the semi-circular sheet in half as shown in Fig. 2.15 to form a quarter circle. 4. Fold the sheet again as shown in Figs. 2.16 and 2.17. 5. Continue with another half fold as shown in Fig. 2.18. 6. Unfold and mark the creases as OB, OC, ..., etc., as shown in Fig. 2.19 and Fig. 2.20.
1. Circle = 360°; half fold gives 180° (write 180° at left bottom corner)
2. Quarter circle gives 90° (mark at top)
3. Next fold gives 45° and 135°
4. Next fold gives 22.5°, 67.5°, 112.5°, 157.5°
Answer: Open-ended craft. Resulting marks on the semicircle: 0°, 22.5°, 45°, 67.5°, 90°, 112.5°, 135°, 157.5°, 180°.

item.question: The measure of a quarter circle is 1/4 of a full turn. The measure of a 1/4 turn = 1/4 of 360° is ________. Or, the measure of a 1/4 turn = 1/2 of a half turn = 1/2 of 180° is ______. Thus, mark 90° at the top of the semicircle.
item.question_tex: The measure of a quarter circle is $\frac{1}{4}$ of a full turn. The measure of the $\frac{1}{4}$ turn $= \frac{1}{4}$ of $360^\circ$ is $\underline{\hspace{1.2em}}$. Or, the measure of the $\frac{1}{4}$ turn $= \frac{1}{2}$ of a half turn $= \frac{1}{2}$ of $180^\circ$ is $\underline{\hspace{1.2em}}$. Thus, mark $90^\circ$ at the top of the semicircle.
item.text: The measure of a quarter circle is $\frac{1}{4}$ of a full turn. The measure of the $\frac{1}{4}$ turn $= \frac{1}{4}$ of $360^\circ$ is $\underline{\hspace{1.2em}}$. item.question: The measure of a quarter circle is 1/4 of a full turn. The measure of a 1/4 turn = 1/4 of 360° is ________. Or, the measure of a 1/4 turn = 1/2 of a half turn = 1/2 of 180° is ______. Thus, mark 90° at the top of the semicircle.

$2$. $\frac{1}{2}$ of $180$ is $90$

item.answer_tex: $22.5^\circ$. The straight angle of $180^\circ$ is divided into eight equal parts, so each angle $= \frac{180}{8} = 22.5^\circ$.
item.answer: 22.5°. The straight angle of 180° is divided into eight equal parts, so each angle = 180/8 = 22.5°.
item.text:
